title: Commit message
when: The user asks for a commit message, or work is ready to commit and needs a clear description of the change.
inputs: the diff or a summary of changes
the project commit convention if any
prompt:
Goal: A commit message with a precise subject and a body that explains why, readable in a one line log.
Steps:
1. Read the diff and name the single main change; if there are several unrelated changes, suggest separate commits.
2. Subject: imperative mood, up to about 50 to 72 characters, no trailing period ("Fix rounding in invoice totals").
3. Follow the project convention if it has one (for example "fix(cart): ..." prefixes); otherwise plain subject lines.
4. Leave one blank line, then a body wrapped at about 72 columns: the problem, why this approach, side effects.
5. Add references at the end (Fixes #123) and a BREAKING CHANGE: line when behavior changes for users.
6. Mention tests added or how it was verified when useful.
Quality bar:
- The subject says what changed, the body says why.
- Specific nouns: file, function or feature names.
- No filler like "update stuff" or "misc".
Pitfalls:
- Describing how the code works line by line.
- Past tense subjects ("Fixed").
- One commit message for many unrelated changes.
Verify:
- [ ] Subject is imperative and short.
- [ ] Blank line between subject and body.
- [ ] Body explains the reason.
- [ ] No placeholder text.
Output: The commit message as plain text, ready for git commit -F or the editor.

examples.input: gera a mensagem de commit pra essa mudança
examples.output: Fix double submit on checkout form / body: button disabled while pending; re-enabled in finally
